title: SSC CPO: combine written revision with physical-stage planning
description: Plan CPO revision by section, avoid expired correction-window advice and prepare for the physical and English demands of later stages.
intro: SSC’s 1 October notice schedules CPO 2026 for 20–28 November. Applications and the 8–10 October correction window have closed. Use this period to test your written preparation and understand the later physical, medical and document requirements; the exam window is not an admit-card release.

sections.title: Build the mock around the current notice
sections.body:
Do not carry a previous year's timer or paper structure into a new cycle without checking. Read the current CPO notification and your admission instructions, then configure practice accordingly. A section that locks when time ends cannot borrow spare time from your best subject.

Keep separate lines for reasoning, awareness, maths and English: attempted, correct, guessed and unfinished. Review unanswered questions after the timer. If you solve them easily without pressure, work on question selection; if not, return to the concept. The [pattern page](/exams/ssc-cpo/exam-pattern/) is a convenient summary, while the official notification remains authoritative.

sections.title: Repair two bottlenecks instead of rereading everything
sections.body:
Choose one slow process and one recurring accuracy error. For example, compare ratios without unnecessary decimal division, and underline the base in a percentage question. Then test the repair on a mixed set where the method is not named.

For English, alternate a grammar review with a short comprehension exercise. Write the sentence or passage evidence supporting the answer. For awareness, close the notes and retrieve a small set of facts before checking them. An hour spent correcting a repeated error can be more useful than finishing another mock with the same mistake.

sections.title: Understand the later physical and medical hurdles
sections.body:
Read the standards and endurance tasks for your sex, category, region and preferred post. A qualifying physical stage still matters: written marks do not erase an unmet eligibility requirement. Check any additional post-specific conditions, including required documents or licences, in the notification.

Plan suitable preparation early and within your experience; this is not a prescribed exercise programme. Review certificates supporting claimed relaxations before the reporting stage. Do not wait for a shortlist to discover that you have been using the wrong physical-standard chart. Use the official notice rather than a single social-media graphic.

sections.title: Keep English and document readiness in the weekly plan
sections.body:
Continue language work while waiting for later-stage dates. Read a passage, summarise its argument and explain why close alternatives are unsupported. The [reading-comprehension guide](/study-guides/reading-comprehension-find-evidence/) gives an original worked example.

Store your application and identity details together. Check the [CPO process page](/exams/ssc-cpo/admit-card/) for the official release workflow. An old correction link is not a current chance to change the application. If a genuine problem remains, use SSC's stated contact process and retain the response rather than trusting an unofficial “edit service”.

drills.prompt: A ratio changes from 3:4 to 4:5. Which is larger?
drills.explanation: Compare 3 × 5 = 15 with 4 × 4 = 16. Thus 3/4 is less than 4/5; decimal division is unnecessary.

drills.prompt: Your total mock score rose while English accuracy fell. What should you inspect?
drills.answer: The section-level error and guessing record.
drills.explanation: A better total can conceal a weak section. Diagnose the language errors before interpreting the whole-paper improvement as readiness.

checklist: Repair one slow method and one recurring error.
Read the physical and post-specific conditions.
Continue English practice while monitoring official notices.

sources.label: SSC official notices and candidate portal

faqs.q: Is the October correction window still open?
faqs.a: The published 8–10 October 2026 window has ended. Check SSC for any explicit further notice.

faqs.q: Does the 20–28 November window give my reporting time?
faqs.a: No. Your individual admission certificate gives your date, shift, centre and reporting instructions.
